model.name: Obligation / Commitment
model.purpose: Reusable mixin for a directed obligation or commitment: bound party, required action or forbearance, conditions of applicability, performance window, and recorded fulfilment or failure.
model.scope_statement: This mixin is the format-neutral context an agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate a single directed obligation or commitment and its fulfilment trail. It covers identity, deontic kind, conferring source, party roles, prescribed action or forbearance, conditions, due time, lifecycle state, performance quality, excuse, violation, secondary consequence duties, evidence, recognition overlays and interoperability alignments. It is mixed into agreements, policies, regulations, access-control decisions and operational records. It does not own party master data, the full contract instrument, the process engine, the general ledger, or permission/prohibition as first-class siblings. Storage formats and access interfaces are projections, not semantics.
in_scope: Identity and cross-system identifiers of an obligation or commitment instance
Deontic classification including contractual, legal, constructive, regulatory, policy-duty and access-control obligation senses
Conferring instrument, clause, authority and legal source
Obligor/bearer, obligee, beneficiary, assigner/assignee and auxiliary-party roles
Required action, forbearance, target object or state, and action refinements
Conditions, constraints, refinements and conditions precedent that make the obligation active
Due time, performance period, reasonable-time fallback, order of performance and place/manner where they bind
Lifecycle states and dual timestamps for event time versus observation time
Fulfilment, partial, defective and late performance, withholding, cure and excused non-performance
Violation, infringement, consequence, remedy, reparation and penalty duties
Evidence, validation, probability/amount recognition overlays, access, retention and standard alignments
out_of_scope: Party, organisation or agent master identity, which belongs in a composable Party/Agent sibling
The full agreement, contract or policy document as an instrument, which confers commitments but is not itself this mixin
Permission, prohibition, licence or Hohfeld claim-right as first-class deontic operators except as correlatives of this mixin
Workflow, task or work-item execution engines that operationalise an action
General-ledger posting, chart of accounts and financial-statement presentation beyond an alignment overlay for present-obligation recognition
Dispute, litigation, arbitration or enforcement case management
Calendar, business-day and holiday-schedule master data
Asset/resource master identity except as a referenced target of the required action

boundary_notes.distinction: FIBO defines an agreement as a negotiated understanding that confers commitments; UNIDROIT and IFRS 15 treat contracts as the instrument that contains performance obligations. This mixin is each conferred commitment unit, not the instrument, the offer/acceptance event, or the document.

ODRL separates Permission, Prohibition and Duty. LegalRuleML treats Obligation, Permission, Prohibition and Right as distinct deontic specifications, with Right implying obligations on auxiliary parties. This mixin is the duty/commitment side only; permissions are a sibling deontic model.

ODRL constraints refine when a Duty is active; LegalRuleML antecedents condition applicability; IAS 37 contingent obligations depend on future events. Conditions are not the obligation; they gate activation and fulfilment.

Fulfilment is evidenced by events that exercise the required action. The obligation is the enduring deontic state; the event is the occurrence. ODRL Evaluator checks whether intended action performance has been met; UNIDROIT judges performance quality against the obligation, not against an event type.

IAS 37 recognises a provision only for a present legal or constructive obligation with probable outflow and reliable estimate. That is a measurement and disclosure overlay on some obligations, not the deontic record itself, and it excludes remote contingencies.

XACML Obligation is an operation the PEP must perform in conjunction with Permit or Deny. HL7 ObligationPolicy and FHIR Obligation codes are mandated workflow or conformance behaviours, not a contractual duty. They align as a specialised obligation sense and must not be merged silently with legal or commercial commitments.

IFRS 15 performance obligations are promises to transfer distinct goods or services to a customer, satisfied when control transfers. They are a revenue-recognition specialisation of contractual commitments, not a general deontic model, and onerous-contract testing remains under IAS 37.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Normative Party, Action, Duty, Constraint, obligation/duty/consequence/remedy properties, fulfilment semantics and Evaluator/Validator roles for policy obligations.

sources.title: LegalRuleML Core Specification Version 1.0
sources.relevance: Normative legal Obligation as a deontic specification with Bearer, AuxiliaryParty, Violation, Compliance, Penalty, Reparation, temporal characteristics and prescriptive statements.

sources.title: FIBO Foundations Agreements Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines Agreement, Commitment, UnilateralCommitment, CommitmentAtLarge, Obligor, Obligee, Beneficiary and hasObligation, including time-bound conferral of commitments.

sources.title: UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts — Chapter 7 Section 1 Non-Performance in General
sources.organization: International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT)
sources.relevance: Defines non-performance including defective and late performance, interference, withholding, cure, additional period, and excused non-performance including force majeure.

sources.title: IAS 37 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.version_or_date: Standard 2026 Issued (IAS 37 originally 1998; onerous-contract amendment May 2020)
sources.relevance: Present legal or constructive obligation, probable outflow, reliable estimate, contingent liability, onerous contract and measurement of uncertain obligations.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Defines Obligation as an operation specified in a rule, policy or policy set that should be performed by the PEP in conjunction with enforcing an authorization decision.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Obligation Codes and ObligationPolicy
sources.relevance: Application and privacy-workflow obligations (SHALL/SHOULD/MAY; encrypt, anonymize) distinct from contractual duties; cites XACML and ISO 22600-2.

sources.title: IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.relevance: Identification of performance obligations as distinct promises and satisfaction by transfer of control over time or at a point in time; defers onerous testing to IAS 37.

sources.title: Data Product Ontology (DPROD) Duty profile
sources.relevance: ODRL profile adding deadline, subjectOfDuty, objectOfDuty and dutyState vocabulary Pending/Active/Fulfilled/Violated; treated as emerging alignment, not W3C core.

sources.title: UNIDROIT Principles 2016 English black-letter
sources.organization: International Institute for the Unification of Private Law (UNIDROIT)
sources.relevance: Article 6.1.1 time of performance (fixed time, period, or reasonable time) and Article 7.1.1 non-performance definition, plus performance and termination remedies.

bundles.name: Identity, deontic kind and conferring source
bundles.description: How an obligation or commitment is identified, classified by deontic and legal kind, and traced to the instrument and authority that conferred it.
bundles.rationale: Agents cannot operate a mixin without a stable identifier, a declared sense of 'obligation' across conflicting standards, and a pointer to the conferring source. ODRL requires uid on policies and optional uid on rules; LegalRuleML uses key/iri; FIBO uses IRIs; XACML uses ObligationId.

layers.name: Identity and identifiers
layers.description: Master-system identifiers, governed IRIs and Dimension-assigned UUID/ULID for the obligation instance and its rule fragments.

findings.name: Obligation instance identity
findings.description: An obligation or commitment instance needs an authoritative identifier in the system of record, optionally a governed IRI for cross-system reference, and a Dimension UUID/ULID when no master id exists. Dates are not identifiers. ODRL Policy MUST have uid IRI; Rules MAY have uid so a Duty can be referenced once by several Permissions. LegalRuleML nodes have internal key and optional iri. XACML Obligation has an identifier.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier of this obligation instance, and which system of record minted it?
What governed global IRI or uid identifies this obligation for cross-system reference, and is it the ODRL rule uid, LegalRuleML iri, XACML ObligationId or another namespace?
If no master or governed identifier exists, what UUID or ULID did the adopting Dimension assign, and when was that assignment observed?
What local keys, clause numbers or policy fragment identifiers must be retained as aliases without being treated as the primary identity?

data_elements.name: Master system identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the authoritative system of record for this obligation instance.

data_elements.name: Governed IRI or uid
data_elements.description: Global IRI for the obligation or Duty/Obligation rule, such as odrl uid or LegalRuleML iri.

data_elements.name: Dimension UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Adopting Dimension assigned identifier used only when no master or governed id exists.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Scheme or namespace that interprets the master or governed identifier.

data_elements.name: Alias keys
data_elements.description: Non-primary local keys including clause numbers and policy fragment identifiers.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is reference data: identifiers, schemes and aliases. No separate artefact is required unless the minting system issues a registration certificate, which would belong to provenance rather than identity.

layers.name: Classification and deontic kind
layers.description: Which sense of obligation applies, its deontic strength, and whether it is achievement, maintenance, forbearance or a specialised policy/access/conformance obligation.

findings.name: Deontic kind and strength
findings.description: Standards use the same English word for different kinds. ODRL Duty is the obligation to exercise an agreed Action. LegalRuleML Obligation is a deontic specification for a state, act or course of action to which a Bearer is legally bound, non-performance of which is a Violation; Prohibition is obligation of the negation. FIBO Commitment is a promise to act or refrain. FHIR Obligation codes qualify SHALL/SHOULD/MAY application behaviour. LegalRuleML examples distinguish modalities such as achievementObligation. These kinds must be classified explicitly and treated as alignments, not as a single merged class.

questions.text: Is this instance a contractual or legal obligation, an ODRL Duty, an XACML/PEP obligation, a FHIR conformance obligation, a constructive obligation, or another declared kind?
What is the deontic strength and modality, including mandatory versus recommended versus permitted-to-the-contrary, and achievement versus maintenance versus forbearance?
If accounting or legal recognition is in play, is the obligation legal, constructive, or only contingent on a future event not wholly within the entity's control?
If the required content is a forbearance, is it modelled as Obligation of a negated act (LegalRuleML [OBL]-p / [FOR]p) rather than as a first-class Prohibition sibling?

data_elements.name: Deontic kind code
data_elements.description: Declared sense of the obligation (contractual, legal, odrl-duty, xacml-obligation, fhir-conformance, constructive, contingent).

data_elements.name: Deontic strength
data_elements.description: Strength such as SHALL, SHOULD, MAY or LegalRuleML obligation versus weak permission.

data_elements.name: Modality code
data_elements.description: Achievement, maintenance, course-of-action or other declared modality.

data_elements.name: Forbearance flag
data_elements.description: True when the commitment is to refrain from acting.

data_elements.name: Constructive obligation indicator
data_elements.description: True when the obligation arises from the entity's actions creating a valid expectation, per IAS 37.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is coded metadata on the mixin instance. Kind schemes are referenced vocabularies, not stored artefacts.

layers.name: Conferring source and authority
layers.description: The legal source, agreement, policy or past event that conferred the commitment and the authority that endorses it.

findings.name: Conferring instrument and authority
findings.description: LegalRuleML binds norms to LegalSources endorsed by an Authority. FIBO agreements confer commitments and are time-bound. IAS 37 requires a past event that creates a present obligation. The mixin must point at the conferring instrument, clause, authority and, where relevant, the past event, without ingesting the whole instrument.

questions.text: Which instrument, policy, statute, judgement or agreement confers this obligation, and which clause or article?
Which authority endorsed the legal source or issued the policy, and in which jurisdiction or profile does it apply?
What past event, if any, created the present obligation, and is existence still contingent on a future event not wholly within the obligated party's control?
Who recorded the link from source to obligation, when was the source observed, and what version of the source was used?

data_elements.name: Source instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the conferring agreement, policy, statute or other legal source.

data_elements.name: Clause locator
data_elements.description: Article, section or clause identifier within the instrument.

data_elements.name: Endorsing authority
data_elements.description: Authority that endorsed the legal source or issued the policy.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction code
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction or legal system in which the source is claimed to operate.

data_elements.name: Past event reference
data_elements.description: Past event giving rise to a present obligation.

data_elements.name: Source observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the source version was observed or ingested, distinct from the event time of conferral.

artifacts.name: Source instrument excerpt
artifacts.description: Excerpt or immutable snapshot of the conferring clause, policy fragment or LegalSource used to interpret the obligation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer the source system's document identifier and version; else governed IRI of the LegalSource; else Dimension UUID of the excerpt plus SHA-256 of bytes.

bundles.name: Parties and directed roles
bundles.description: Who is bound to perform, to whom the obligation is owed, and which other functional roles participate, including transfer and third-party benefit.
bundles.rationale: Every consulted primary model is role-directed. ODRL assigner/assignee, LegalRuleML Bearer/AuxiliaryParty, FIBO Obligor/Obligee/Beneficiary, DPROD subjectOfDuty/objectOfDuty. Party master data remains a sibling; this mixin stores roles and references.

layers.name: Bound and entitled parties
layers.description: Obligor/bearer who must perform and obligee/beneficiary who is entitled to performance or its outcome.

findings.name: Obligor or bearer
findings.description: FIBO Obligor is a party bound legally or by agreement to repay, pay, do something or refrain, and hasObligation some Commitment. ODRL assignee is the party required to fulfil an agreed Duty and MUST have the ability to exercise the Duty Action. LegalRuleML Bearer is the role to which a Deontic Specification is primarily directed. Collections of parties are allowed in ODRL PartyCollection.

questions.text: Which party or party collection is bound to perform this obligation, and in which role (obligor, bearer, assignee, subjectOfDuty)?
Does the bound party have the capacity and ability to exercise the required action, as ODRL requires of the obligated party?
If multiple parties are bound, is the duty joint, several, or joint-and-several, and how is performance by one credited to the others?
Has the bound party been substituted, delegated or novated, and who remains liable after the change?

data_elements.name: Obligor party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party or agent bound to perform.

data_elements.name: Obligor role code
data_elements.description: Functional role label such as obligor, bearer, assignee or subjectOfDuty.

data_elements.name: Capacity to perform
data_elements.description: Whether the bound party currently has ability/capacity to exercise the action.

data_elements.name: Multiplicity of obligors
data_elements.description: Joint, several or joint-and-several binding among co-obligors.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Party identity lives in the Party sibling; this finding stores role codes and references only.

findings.name: Obligee, beneficiary and correlative right
findings.description: FIBO Obligee is the party to whom a commitment or obligation is owed; Beneficiary receives benefit or profit. ODRL assigner issues the Rule and may require the Duty. LegalRuleML Right gives Permission to a Bearer and implies Obligations or Prohibitions on AuxiliaryParty. FIBO treats obligations and rights as reciprocal aspects of a commitment. The entitled party is therefore a first-class role of this mixin, while the right itself remains a sibling.

questions.text: To whom is this obligation owed, and is that party the obligee, compensated party, assigner, or objectOfDuty?
Is there a beneficiary distinct from the obligee, including third-party benefit or a commitment at large without identified beneficiaries?
What correlative right, claim or permission does the entitled party hold, and is it recorded in a sibling Right/Permission model rather than duplicated here?
Which auxiliary parties bear related obligations or prohibitions so that a right-holder can eventually exercise the right?

data_elements.name: Obligee party reference
data_elements.description: Party to whom the commitment or obligation is owed.

data_elements.name: Beneficiary references
data_elements.description: Parties that receive the outcome or benefit of performance.

data_elements.name: Commitment at large flag
data_elements.description: True when the commitment is made without direct involvement of potential beneficiaries, as in FIBO CommitmentAtLarge.

data_elements.name: Correlative right reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the sibling right or permission implied by this duty.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Roles and correlative links are references to Party and Right siblings, not independent artefacts.

bundles.name: Action, object and conditions
bundles.description: What must be done or refrained from, on which object or state, and under which conditions the duty is active.
bundles.rationale: ODRL Duty MUST have an Action and MAY have target Asset, refinements and constraints. LegalRuleML Obligation applies to a state, act or course of action under antecedent conditions. FIBO commitments are to act or refrain. UNIDROIT distinguishes monetary and non-monetary obligations.

layers.name: Required action, forbearance and object
layers.description: The obligatory operation or state and the asset, person or state that is its object.

findings.name: Required action or forbearance
findings.description: ODRL interprets Action as obligatory when related to a Duty; refinements such as payAmount and unit specialise the action. FIBO includes refrain-from-acting. UNIDROIT 7.2.1/7.2.2 distinguish monetary payment from other performance, with impossibility and personal-character limits on specific performance. IFRS 15 identifies distinct goods or services as performance obligations. The mixin records the required content without owning the Action catalogue.

questions.text: What action, state or course of action is required, and is it drawn from ODRL Action, an IFRS 15 promised good or service, a monetary payment, or a local action catalogue?
What refinements quantify or specialise the action, such as amount, unit, count, quality metric or manner?
Is the obligation monetary or non-monetary, and are specific-performance exceptions (impossibility, unreasonable burden, cover from another source, exclusively personal character) declared?
On which asset, person, data set or state must the action be exercised, and is that target owned by a sibling Asset/Party model?

data_elements.name: Action code
data_elements.description: Identifier of the required operation or state, for example odrl:compensate or a local catalogue code.

data_elements.name: Action scheme
data_elements.description: Vocabulary or profile that defines the action code.

data_elements.name: Action refinements
data_elements.description: Constraint-like refinements on the action such as payAmount, unit, count.

data_elements.name: Monetary obligation flag
data_elements.description: True when the required performance is payment of money.

data_elements.name: Target object reference
data_elements.description: Asset, party or state that is the primary object of the required action.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Action codes, refinements and target references are inline structured data; catalogues and assets are siblings.

layers.name: Conditions, constraints and activation
layers.description: Boolean, temporal, spatial and event conditions that determine whether the obligation is active and whether fulfilment is possible.

findings.name: Conditions, constraints and conditions precedent
findings.description: ODRL Rules MAY include constraints that MUST all be satisfied for the Duty to be fulfilled; logical constraints include andSequence with preserved order. Constraints on Rules determine if a rule is Active. LegalRuleML antecedents condition applicability of the deontic consequent. IAS 37 contingent obligations depend on uncertain future events not wholly within the entity's control. FIBO LegalCapacity (snippet only) names condition precedent and contingent obligation; that ontology was not fully fetched and is recorded as a gap for detailed clause-linkage properties.

questions.text: Which conditions or constraints must be satisfied for this obligation to be active, and are they conjunctive, disjunctive or sequenced?
Is there a condition precedent, concurrent condition or condition subsequent, and which clause or event supplies it?
Does a spatial, jurisdictional or delivery-channel constraint limit where or how the action may be exercised?
If a time or event constraint can no longer be satisfied after missed performance, may the original duty still be marked fulfilable once a consequence is triggered, as ODRL recommends?

data_elements.name: Constraints
data_elements.description: Boolean or logical constraints that refine the duty or its action.

data_elements.name: Logical operand
data_elements.description: How multiple constraints combine, including andSequence.

data_elements.name: Condition kind
data_elements.description: Precedent, concurrent, subsequent or contingent-future-event.

data_elements.name: Spatial or channel constraint
data_elements.description: Named area, coordinates, jurisdiction or delivery channel limiting the duty.

data_elements.name: Active under constraints
data_elements.description: Whether all applicability constraints are currently satisfied.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Conditions are structured expressions referencing events, times and sibling constraint models; they are not independent artefacts.

bundles.name: Time, place and performance regime
bundles.description: When performance is due, in what order relative to reciprocal duties, and where or how it must be tendered.
bundles.rationale: UNIDROIT 6.1.1 fixes time of performance as a point, a period, or a reasonable time after conclusion. ODRL uses dateTime and related left operands as constraints. DPROD adds absolute or relative deadlines. UNIDROIT 7.1.3 couples withholding to simultaneous or consecutive performance.

layers.name: Due time and performance window
layers.description: Point due, interval due, relative duration from activation, and reasonable-time fallback, with explicit timezone.

findings.name: Due date and performance window
findings.description: UNIDROIT 6.1.1: if a time is fixed or determinable, perform at that time; if a period is fixed, at any time within it unless the other party chooses; otherwise within a reasonable time after conclusion. ODRL dateTime constraints bound when a rule is active or must be exercised. DPROD deadline allows xsd:dateTime or xsd:duration relative to activation. Event time of due instant and observation time of the due-date record must be separate. A date is not an identifier.

questions.text: Is performance due at a point in time, at any time within a period, within a duration from activation, or within a reasonable time, and who may choose the time within a period?
What RFC 3339 offset or Z, business calendar and close-of-business convention apply to the due instant or window?
Is this a one-shot duty or a recurring series, and which sibling schedule model owns the recurrence if any?
When did the due time become known (event time of agreement or notice) versus when was it ingested into this record (observation time)?

data_elements.name: Due-form code
data_elements.description: Point, period, relative-duration or reasonable-time.

data_elements.name: Due instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset or Z for a point due time.

data_elements.name: Performance window start
data_elements.description: Start of a period in which performance may occur.

data_elements.name: Performance window end
data_elements.description: End of a period in which performance may occur.

data_elements.name: Relative duration
data_elements.description: Duration from activation used to compute a deadline.

data_elements.name: Due-date observation time
data_elements.description: When the due time was ingested or last confirmed, distinct from the due instant itself.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Due times are typed timestamps and durations. Recurring schedules belong to a sibling schedule model and are referenced, not copied.

layers.name: Order, place and manner of performance
layers.description: Simultaneous versus consecutive performance, withholding rights, and place or manner constraints.

findings.name: Order, location and manner
findings.description: UNIDROIT 7.1.3: where parties perform simultaneously either may withhold until the other tenders; where consecutive, the later party may withhold until the first has performed. ODRL spatial and virtualLocation left operands can constrain place. Manner may appear as action refinements. Place is relevant only when the duty is location-sensitive.

questions.text: Must this obligation be performed simultaneously with, before, or after named reciprocal obligations, and may performance be withheld until the counterpart tenders?
Where must performance be tendered, including named place, geospatial area, virtual location or delivery channel?
What manner, form or medium of performance is required, and is earlier or partial tender acceptable?

data_elements.name: Order of performance
data_elements.description: Simultaneous, consecutive-before, consecutive-after or independent.

data_elements.name: Reciprocal obligation references
data_elements.description: Other obligations whose tender gates this one.

data_elements.name: Withholding allowed
data_elements.description: Whether the bound party may withhold this performance until the counterpart tenders.

data_elements.name: Place of performance
data_elements.description: Named place, area or virtual location of tender.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Order and place are coded relations and references to location and sibling obligation records.

bundles.name: Fulfilment, lifecycle and excuse
bundles.description: States of the duty, what counts as performance, and when non-performance is excused, curable or still a failure.
bundles.rationale: ODRL Duty is fulfilled if constraints are satisfied and the action with refinements has been exercised. UNIDROIT treats defective and late performance as non-performance and provides cure, additional period, interference and force majeure. DPROD proposes Pending/Active/Fulfilled/Violated as an evaluation vocabulary, which is an emerging profile not W3C core.

layers.name: Lifecycle states and transitions
layers.description: Declared state machine for the obligation instance and who may change it.

findings.name: Lifecycle and state transitions
findings.description: ODRL defines fulfilled for Duty/obligation, infringed/not infringed for Prohibition, and active via satisfied constraints. LegalRuleML records Compliance and Violation as indications plus TemporalCharacteristic pairing Time with Legal Status and Status Development. DPROD names Pending, Active, Fulfilled, Violated as canonical evaluation states; that vocabulary is a profile and a gap if adopted as if it were ODRL core. Additional operational states used in practice include waived, discharged, expired, suspended and transferred, which lack a single primary standard and must be declared locally.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle or evaluation state of this obligation, and which state vocabulary (ODRL, LegalRuleML, DPROD profile, or local) is being used?
At what event time did the state become true, and at what observation time was that state recorded or ingested?
Who is authorised to assert fulfilment, violation, waiver, discharge or suspension, and under which policy?
If LegalRuleML temporal characteristics apply, what legal status and status development hold at each recorded time?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Current state such as pending, active, fulfilled, violated, waived, discharged, expired or suspended.

data_elements.name: State vocabulary
data_elements.description: Vocabulary IRI or code for the state series in use.

data_elements.name: State event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time when the state actually obtained.

data_elements.name: State observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time when the state was recorded or ingested.

data_elements.name: Transition actor
data_elements.description: Party or system that asserted the latest state change.

findings.inline_only_rationale: State is inline coded data with dual timestamps. Authorising policies are referenced siblings.

layers.name: Performance quality, satisfaction and excuse
layers.description: Whether the action was exercised as required, including partial, defective and late performance, IFRS 15 satisfaction, and excused non-performance.

findings.name: Performance, satisfaction and excuse
findings.description: ODRL fulfilment is exercise of the action with refinements and constraints satisfied. UNIDROIT 7.1.1 treats failure, defective performance and late performance as non-performance, including both excused and non-excused cases. 7.1.2 removes the quality of non-performance where caused by the other party's act or allocated risk. 7.1.4 allows cure after notice; 7.1.5 allows an additional period. IFRS 15 satisfaction occurs when the customer obtains control, over time or at a point in time. These tests conflict and must be recorded separately rather than collapsed.

questions.text: Has the obligated party exercised the required action with all refinements satisfied and all constraints satisfied, in the ODRL sense?
Was performance complete, partial, defective or late under UNIDROIT 7.1.1, and is that failure excused by interference, allocated risk or force majeure?
If this is a revenue performance obligation, is it satisfied over time or at a point in time, and has the customer obtained control?
Has a cure notice or additional period for performance been given, and did the non-performing party cure promptly at its own expense?
What measure of progress toward complete satisfaction is being used, and is there an enforceable right to payment for performance to date?

data_elements.name: Action exercised
data_elements.description: Whether the Duty action has been exercised in the ODRL sense.

data_elements.name: Performance quality
data_elements.description: Complete, partial, defective, late or none.

data_elements.name: Excuse code
data_elements.description: Interference, allocated-risk, force-majeure, withholding or none.

data_elements.name: Satisfaction pattern
data_elements.description: Over-time or point-in-time for IFRS 15 performance obligations.

data_elements.name: Progress measure
data_elements.description: Method and value for progress toward complete satisfaction.

artifacts.name: Cure or additional-period notice
artifacts.description: Notice indicating proposed manner and timing of cure, or granting an additional period for performance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Notice identifier assigned by the issuing party system; else Dimension UUID plus RFC 3339 issued-at.

bundles.name: Violation, consequences and secondary duties
bundles.description: How failure is indicated and which additional duties, remedies, reparations or penalties then bind, including nested consequence chains.
bundles.rationale: ODRL consequence Duties become additional requirements while the original duty remains to be fulfilled; remedy Duties address prohibition infringement. LegalRuleML Violation triggers Penalty and Reparation statements, including reparative obligations that can chain. UNIDROIT supplies termination and damages as remedies for non-performance without encoding them as nested Duties.

layers.name: Violation and non-performance indication
layers.description: Recorded failure indications distinct from lifecycle state codes.

findings.name: Violation and non-performance
findings.description: LegalRuleML Violation indicates that an Obligation or Prohibition has been violated; Compliance indicates an Obligation has been fulfilled or a Prohibition not violated. ODRL treats unexercised Duty action as unfulfilled and prohibition exercise as infringement. UNIDROIT non-performance is broader than binary violation. A recorded indication must name the standard used, the time of failure, and whether it is fundamental for termination purposes.

questions.text: Has a violation, infringement or non-performance been indicated, under which standard, and at what event time versus observation time?
Does the failure amount to fundamental non-performance entitling termination under UNIDROIT 7.3.1, or only to damages or withholding?
Has a LegalRuleML Compliance indication been asserted, and does it cover the original duty, consequence duties, or both?

data_elements.name: Violation indicated
data_elements.description: Whether a violation or equivalent failure indication is currently asserted.

data_elements.name: Failure kind
data_elements.description: Violation, infringement, non-performance, late, defective or none.

data_elements.name: Failure event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time when the failure obtained.

data_elements.name: Fundamental non-performance flag
data_elements.description: Whether the failure is treated as fundamental for termination.

artifacts.name: Default or violation notice
artifacts.description: Notice asserting non-performance, infringement or termination.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Issuer notice identifier; else Dimension UUID plus issued-at timestamp.

layers.name: Consequence, remedy, reparation and penalty
layers.description: Nested or sibling duties that bind because the primary duty failed or a prohibition was infringed.

findings.name: Consequence, remedy, reparation and penalty
findings.description: ODRL consequence is a sub-property of failure: if a Permission duty or Policy obligation is not fulfilled, consequence Duties ALSO become requirements and the original MUST still be fulfilled; consequence MUST NOT nest on a Duty that is already a consequence; remedy MUST NOT refer to a Duty that includes a consequence. LegalRuleML PenaltyStatement and ReparationStatement follow violation, and reparative obligations can activate further rules. Secondary duties are child or referenced obligation instances, not free text.

questions.text: Which consequence, remedy, reparation or penalty duties are attached, and are they child obligations or references to separately governed instances?
Must the original duty still be fulfilled together with all consequence duties, including after a date constraint has become unsatisfiable?
Is further chaining prohibited because this duty is already a consequence or because a remedy points at a duty that itself has a consequence?
What sanction, correction or agreed payment for non-performance is specified, and is it a LegalRuleML Penalty or a liquidated amount?

data_elements.name: Secondary duty references
data_elements.description: Child or referenced obligation instances triggered by failure.

data_elements.name: Secondary duty kind
data_elements.description: Consequence, remedy, reparation or penalty.

data_elements.name: Original still required
data_elements.description: Whether the original duty remains to be fulfilled after consequences attach.

data_elements.name: Is itself a consequence
data_elements.description: True when this instance was created as a consequence or remedy of another duty.

data_elements.name: Penalty or agreed payment
data_elements.description: Quantity of a sanction or agreed payment for non-performance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Secondary duties are nested or referenced mixin instances. Penalty amounts are inline quantities; court orders would be artefacts of a dispute sibling, not of this mixin.

bundles.name: Evidence, measurement, access and interoperability
bundles.description: How fulfilment is evidenced and validated, how present obligations are measured, who may access the record, how long it is kept, and how it maps to external standards.
bundles.rationale: ODRL Validator and Evaluator separate schema conformance from performance evaluation. IAS 37 measures provisions at the amount rationally paid to settle or transfer, discounted, and discloses contingencies. XACML obligations travel with authorization decisions. FHIR obligations are interoperability conformance, not legal duties. Access and retention follow the sensitivity of party and commercial data.

layers.name: Evidence and validation
layers.description: Proof of performance and checks that the instance meets model cardinalities and evaluation rules.

findings.name: Fulfilment evidence and validation
findings.description: ODRL distinguishes a Validator (cardinality and type conformance of the Policy expression) from an Evaluator (whether Rules have met intended action performance). LegalRuleML Compliance is an indication, not a proof bundle. Evidence artefacts such as receipts, delivery records, logs or decision responses must be independently identifiable and integrity-protected. Quality of evidence is separate from the deontic state.

questions.text: What evidence artefacts demonstrate that the required action was exercised, and which integrity hash or identifier binds each artefact to this obligation?
Has the instance passed structural validation, and has an evaluator determined that intended performance was met, as distinct checks?
What is the assessed quality or reliability of the evidence, including who produced it and whether it is self-asserted by the obligor?
If fulfilment is asserted without evidence, is that an exception, a waiver, or an invalid state transition?

data_elements.name: Evidence artefact references
data_elements.description: Identifiers of artefacts that support fulfilment or violation.

data_elements.name: Structurally valid
data_elements.description: Whether the instance meets cardinality and type constraints of the adopted profile.

data_elements.name: Performance evaluated
data_elements.description: Whether an evaluator has judged intended action performance.

data_elements.name: Evidence quality
data_elements.description: Assessed reliability of the supporting evidence.

data_elements.name: Self-asserted evidence
data_elements.description: True when evidence is produced solely by the obligated party.

artifacts.name: Fulfilment evidence pack
artifacts.description: Receipt, delivery record, system log, attestation or other proof that the required action was exercised.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Producer-assigned evidence identifier preferred; else Dimension UUID plus SHA-256 of bytes; record producer and produced-at separately from ingestion time.

layers.name: Recognition overlay, access, retention and interoperability
layers.description: Accounting recognition, access-control obligations, retention after discharge, and mappings to external standards.

findings.name: Present-obligation recognition and measurement overlay
findings.description: IAS 37 recognises a provision when a present legal or constructive obligation exists from a past event, outflow is probable, and the amount can be estimated reliably; otherwise a contingent liability is disclosed unless remote. Measurement is the amount rationally paid to settle or transfer, including risk and discounting. Onerous contracts are measured under IAS 37 even when revenue is under IFRS 15. US GAAP constructive-obligation treatment differs and is a recorded conflict, not a claim of this mixin. This overlay must not be mistaken for the deontic record.

questions.text: Does a present legal or constructive obligation exist from a past event, is outflow probable, and can the amount be estimated reliably?
What amount would be rationally paid to settle or transfer the obligation at period end, including risk adjustment and discounting?
If unrecognised, is the item a contingent liability requiring disclosure, and is the possibility of outflow remote?
If the host contract is onerous, what is the cost of fulfilling versus terminating, using incremental costs plus allocation of direct costs per the 2020 IAS 37 amendment?

data_elements.name: Present obligation recognised
data_elements.description: Whether IAS 37 recognition criteria are met.

data_elements.name: Outflow probability
data_elements.description: Assessed probability that settlement will require outflow of resources.

data_elements.name: Settlement amount
data_elements.description: Measured amount of the provision or estimate of financial effect.

data_elements.name: Contingent liability
data_elements.description: True when disclosed but not recognised.

data_elements.name: Measurement basis standard
data_elements.description: IAS 37, US GAAP Topic 450, or other declared basis; not a conformance claim.

artifacts.name: Measurement working paper
artifacts.description: Estimate, discounting and probability working paper supporting a provision or contingent-liability disclosure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Finance-system document id and period-end date as attributes, not as the identifier; Dimension UUID plus content hash for the serial file.

findings.name: Access, retention and interoperability mappings
findings.description: XACML obligations must be fulfilled by the PEP in conjunction with the authorization decision and are identified with attribute assignments. HL7 ObligationPolicy conveys mandated workflow such as encrypt, citing XACML and ISO 22600-2. FHIR Obligation codes express SHALL/SHOULD/MAY handling of content and must not be treated as legal duties. Obligation records contain party and commercial data, so default access is restricted to role-holders, evaluators and auditors. Retention after discharge is a Dimension policy; legal holds are exceptions. Interoperability is by alignment maps, not by claiming dual conformance.

questions.text: Who may read, create, update or delete this obligation record, at bundle, layer, finding and artefact scope, and which PEP obligations apply when access is decided?
If this instance is an access-control obligation, what ObligationId and attribute assignments must the PEP fulfil with the decision, and what happens if it cannot?
How long is the obligation record and its evidence retained after discharge, fulfilment or waiver, and is a legal hold or statutory retention in force?

Which external classes is this instance aligned to (ODRL Duty, LegalRuleML Obligation, FIBO Commitment, IAS 37 provision, IFRS 15 PO, XACML Obligation, FHIR Obligation), and which conflicts are declared rather than hidden?
Does the record contain personal data of parties such that privacy obligations (including HL7 anonymize/encrypt workflow) attach to storage and sharing?

data_elements.name: Access scope
data_elements.description: Granted scopes among bundle, layer, finding and artefact.

data_elements.name: XACML ObligationId
data_elements.description: Identifier of a PEP obligation attached to an authorization decision.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration or end time for keeping the record after terminal state.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: True when deletion is suspended.

data_elements.name: Alignment targets
data_elements.description: External classes this instance is mapped to, without implied conformance.

data_elements.name: Conformance claimed
data_elements.description: True only when a validator has evidence of conformance to a named profile.

artifacts.name: Authorization decision with obligations
artifacts.description: XACML or equivalent decision response carrying Obligation elements to be fulfilled by the PEP.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Decision identifier from the PDP; ObligationId values retained as child identifiers; Dimension UUID if the PDP id is absent.

functions.name: Record commitment or obligation
functions.description: Create a mixin instance from a conferring instrument or explicit declaration, capturing parties, action, conditions and due window without embedding sibling masters.
outputs: obligation instance with Dimension UUID and optional governed IRI
preconditions: at least one bound party reference
effects: new obligation instance exists in pending or active state depending on constraints

functions.name: Evaluate applicability and due status
functions.description: Determine whether constraints are satisfied (rule active), whether the due instant or window has been reached, and whether the obligated party still has ability to perform.
effects: state may move between pending and active
overdue indication may be raised without yet asserting violation

functions.name: Record fulfilment
functions.description: Assert that the required action has been exercised with refinements and constraints satisfied, attaching evidence and dual timestamps.
preconditions: instance is active or an authorised exception applies
evidence present unless a recorded waiver exists
effects: state becomes fulfilled or compliance indicated

functions.name: Record non-performance or violation
functions.description: Record failure including defective or late performance, with optional excuse, fundamental-failure assessment and notices.
preconditions: due window has passed or defective tender has been assessed
effects: state becomes violated or remains active if additional period or cure is running
termination or damages flags may be set without executing those sibling processes

functions.name: Offer cure or grant additional period
functions.description: Apply UNIDROIT 7.1.4 cure or 7.1.5 additional period, suspending inconsistent remedies until the period expires.
inputs: notice of cure or additional period
preconditions: cure is appropriate and notice is timely
effects: aggrieved party may still withhold and claim delay damages

functions.name: Attach consequence, remedy or reparation
functions.description: Bind secondary duties when a primary duty fails or a prohibition is infringed, preserving the original duty unless the profile says otherwise.
outputs: child or referenced secondary obligation instances
preconditions: primary is not already a consequence if ODRL nesting rules apply
effects: original remains required unless an explicit discharge is recorded

functions.name: Discharge, waive or release
functions.description: Bring the obligation to a terminal non-violation state by performance, waiver, release or expiry, with authority and retention clocks.
preconditions: actor has authority to waive or acknowledge discharge
legal hold is not blocking if the action is deletion rather than logical discharge
effects: state becomes discharged, waived or expired
evidence and record retained per policy

functions.name: Enforce access-control obligation
functions.description: Evaluate ObligationExpressions on a Permit or Deny decision and require the PEP to perform the specified operations in conjunction with enforcement.
outputs: decision plus obligation list with ObligationId and attribute assignments
effects: PEP must fulfil listed operations with the decision
access-control obligation sense is recorded distinctly from legal duty

functions.name: Assess present-obligation recognition
functions.description: Apply IAS 37 tests for provision versus contingent liability and optionally IFRS 15 satisfaction measurement, as an overlay on the deontic record.
effects: does not by itself change deontic fulfilment state

composition.purpose: Obligor, obligee, beneficiary, assigner, assignee, bearer and auxiliary parties are references to a party sibling, not copies.
The mixin is conferred by an agreement or contract and is the commitment unit those instruments contain.
Policies group Duties and ObligationExpressions; this mixin is the duty/obligation member, not the policy container.
Required operations are codes in an action vocabulary such as ODRL Action; the mixin does not own the catalogue.
Target of a Duty or performance subject is a referenced asset or resource.
Applicability and refinement constraints are composed into the mixin and may themselves be sibling expressions.
Fulfilment, past-event conferral, cure notices and violations are evidenced by referenced events.
Correlative right or permission implied by a duty; kept as a sibling deontic operator, not merged.
Alignment to W3C ODRL Duty/obligation/consequence/remedy semantics without claiming profile conformance.
Alignment to OASIS legal deontic Obligation, Violation, Compliance, Bearer and Reparation.
Alignment to FIBO Commitment, Obligor, Obligee and agreement conferral.
Optional recognition and measurement overlay for provisions and contingent liabilities.
Specialisation for distinct promises to customers and satisfaction by transfer of control.
Specialised PEP-enforced obligation sense attached to authorization decisions.
Conformance and privacy-workflow obligation sense; explicitly not a legal duty.
Secondary consequence, remedy, reparation or penalty duties nested under a failed primary duty subject to ODRL non-nesting rules.
Recurring obligations reference a sibling schedule rather than encoding calendars here.

owner_package_requirements: Designate an owner package that governs identifier minting, state-transition authority and retention for obligation instances in this Dimension.
Declare the action-code and state-code vocabularies the Dimension will accept, including whether ODRL Common Vocabulary, local catalogues, or both.
Require every instance to carry at least a Dimension UUID/ULID and a declared deontic-kind-code so legal, policy and access-control senses cannot be silently merged.
Publish the list of sibling models that must be referenced (Party, Agreement, Action, Asset, Event) and forbid embedding those masters in this mixin.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Place governed IRIs under the adopting Dimension's namespace, for example {dimension-namespace}/xct/obl/{id}. When mapping, retain foreign uids such as http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/ Duty instances, LegalRuleML iri values, FIBO individual IRIs and XACML ObligationId as aliases, never as overwritten primary keys. Do not use dates, due instants or clause numbers as identifiers.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical instance is the deontic fact set: identity, kind, party role references, action, constraints, due form, state, and links to source, evidence and secondary duties. Serialisations (JSON, XML, RDF, tables) are projections.
Party, asset, instrument and event values are references, not embedded master records.
Timestamps canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z. Dual-field event time and observation/ingestion time are both stored when both are known.
IRIs are stored in absolute form; ODRL compact policies MUST be expandable to the atomic cardinalities of the Information Model before validation.
Deontic-kind-code is mandatory canonical metadata; mappings to ODRL, LegalRuleML, XACML and FHIR are alignment annotations, not replacements of kind.
patch_rules: Patches may add evidence, state transitions, secondary duties, measurement overlays and aliases. They must not silently replace master-system-id, governed-iri or original action/due content without an authorised amendment event.
Due-time changes require an authority reference (amendment clause, notice or court order) and preserve the prior due values in provenance.
Fulfilment assertions without evidence are rejected unless a waiver exception is itself recorded as a patch with actor and time.
Consequence attachment is additive: it patches in child duties and must not delete the original duty unless discharge is separately authorised.
compatibility_rules: Do not claim ODRL profile conformance unless an ODRL Validator has passed the instance against a declared profile IRI.
Do not treat XACML or FHIR Obligation identifiers as legal Duty uids.
IAS 37/IFRS 15 overlay fields are optional and must round-trip without being required by deontic-only consumers.
US GAAP constructive-obligation differences are declared conflicts; a US-GAAP overlay must not overwrite IAS 37 fields.
DPROD dutyState values may be stored as a profile mapping, not as if they were W3C ODRL core.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier from the issuing instrument, PDP, finance system or notice system
Governed global identifier or IRI (ODRL uid, LegalRuleML iri, FIBO IRI, XACML ObligationId)
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event and observation timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record event time and observation/ingestion time separately whenever both exist.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts use {dimension-short}-obl-{instance-id}-{artefact-role}-v{n}.{ext} where artefact-role is source-excerpt, evidence, notice, decision or measurement, and n is a monotonic integer per instance and role.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artefact stores a SHA-256 (or stronger) digest of the uninterpreted bytes, producer identity, produced-at event time and ingested-at observation time; evidence packs cannot be swapped without a new version.

policies: Fulfilment cannot be asserted without linked evidence unless an authorised waiver exception is recorded.
Access-control, legal and contractual senses of obligation MUST keep distinct deontic-kind-code values and MUST NOT be merged in queries by English label alone.
Original duties remain required after consequence attachment unless an explicit discharge is recorded, matching ODRL consequence semantics.
Logical discharge is preferred to physical delete; physical delete is blocked during legal hold and while statutory retention runs.
Constraint evaluation precedes overdue and violation assertions; force-majeure and interference excuses must be coded rather than inferred from silence.

read: Role-holders named on the instance (obligor, obligee, beneficiary), evaluators, and auditors may read by default.
Artefact-scope read may be narrower than finding-scope read when evidence contains personal or commercially sensitive data.
Anonymous or cross-tenant read is denied except for CommitmentAtLarge instruments that the owner has published.
create: Create requires a bound party, a required action or forbearance, a deontic-kind-code and a recorder identity.
Create from instrument parse MUST link source-instrument-ref and source-observed-at.
Create of an XACML-sense obligation MUST include ObligationId and the authorization decision reference.
update: State transitions are append-only patches with actor, event time and observation time.
Amendments to action, due time or parties require authority evidence.
Measurement overlay updates do not by themselves change deontic state.
delete: Physical delete is denied while legal-hold-flag is true or retention-period has not expired.
Logical discharge, waiver or expiry is the default terminal operation.
Cascade delete of child consequence duties is allowed only with the parent and only after retention rules are met.

roles.name: Dimension obligation steward
responsibilities: Own identifier policy, vocabularies, retention and alignment maps
Authorise waivers and exceptional constraint relaxation after missed dates

roles.name: Obligation evaluator
responsibilities: Determine whether constraints are satisfied and whether Rules have met intended action performance, in the ODRL Evaluator sense
Ensure evaluation results (active, overdue, fulfilled, violated) are attributable to a named evaluator or system

roles.name: Structural validator
responsibilities: Check cardinality and type conformance of the policy expression, in the ODRL Validator sense
Withhold any profile-conformance claim until the instance has passed validation against a declared profile IRI

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Read obligation records and audit logs without holding steward authority
Verify that every create, state transition, evidence attach, consequence attach, waiver and delete is logged with actor, event time, observation time and previous state

roles.name: Policy enforcement point
responsibilities: Fulfil the ObligationId operations and attribute assignments carried with a Permit or Deny decision, in conjunction with enforcing that decision
Keep the access-control obligation sense distinct from legal and contractual duties

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Grant least-privilege read to named role-holders and evaluators; grant write of state transitions only to authorised assessors; grant create to instrument-recording systems and policy authors; grant artefact-scope access separately from finding-scope access.
exceptions: Legal hold and regulatory examination may extend read to named investigators without making them stewards.
CommitmentAtLarge public instruments may be read more widely than bilateral duties.
PEP obligation payloads may be visible to runtime enforcement components that are not party to the underlying commercial duty.
audit_requirements: Log every create, state transition, evidence attach, consequence attach, waiver and delete with actor, event time, observation time and previous state.
Audit logs retain ObligationId/uid aliases used at the time of the action.
Evaluation results (active, overdue, fulfilled, violated) are attributable to a named evaluator or system.

read_order: Specification URL resource for this mixin
Processes URL resource for state transitions, evaluation and enforcement
Storage type URL resource for the chosen projection
Interface URL resource for query and patch operations

coverage.claim: Wide-union mixin for party, action, due date, condition and fulfilment, aligned to W3C ODRL Duty, OASIS LegalRuleML Obligation, FIBO Commitment, UNIDROIT performance/non-performance, IAS 37/IFRS 15 recognition overlays, and XACML/HL7 access-conformance senses. This is not a claim of jurisdictional completeness, dual-standard conformance, or a unified deontic logic.

checklist.notes: Master-system id, governed IRI/uid, Dimension UUID/ULID, aliases; dates excluded as identifiers.
Pending/active/fulfilled/violated plus discharge, waiver, expiry, suspension; ODRL, LegalRuleML and DPROD vocabularies distinguished.
Obligor/obligee/beneficiary/auxiliary, reciprocal duties, correlative rights, source instrument, child consequences.
UNIDROIT 6.1.1 due forms, ODRL dateTime, dual event/observation timestamps, recurrence deferred to sibling schedule.
Source observation, recorder, evaluator, evidence producer, past-event conferral.
Dimension steward owns the record; obligee owns the correlative claim; party masters remain sibling-owned.
ODRL Validator versus Evaluator; structural-valid-flag versus performance-evaluated-flag.
Default deny, role-holder read, XACML PEP obligations, artefact-scope versus finding-scope.
Logical discharge default; retention period after terminal state; legal hold exception.
ALIGN maps to ODRL, LegalRuleML, FIBO, IAS 37, IFRS 15, XACML, FHIR; conformance claimed only with evidence.
Mandatory kind code separating legal, contractual, constructive, policy-duty, access-control and conformance senses.
Evidence pack artefact, quality, self-assertion and no-fulfilment-without-evidence policy.
ODRL constraints, LegalRuleML antecedents, IAS 37 contingency; FIBO LegalCapacity condition-precedent properties only snippet-level and flagged as a gap.
FIBO Obligor/Obligee/Beneficiary, ODRL assigner/assignee, LegalRuleML Bearer/AuxiliaryParty.
ODRL consequence/remedy nesting limits and LegalRuleML reparative chaining.

known_omissions: FIBO FND Law LegalCapacity contingent-obligation and condition-precedent properties were only snippet-searched, not fetched as a full ontology, so clause-linkage details are a gap.
Assignment, delegation and novation of obligations are not specified in the fetched UNIDROIT chapter 7 section 1; likely belong to a sibling transfer/novation model.
Joint and several liability multiplicity is asked but not grounded in a primary multiplicity scheme beyond FIBO party-role cardinality.
Prescription, limitation periods and death/incapacity of the obligor lack primary support in the fetched set.
CISG Article 33 (time of performance) is the acknowledged inspiration for UNIDROIT 6.1.1 but was not fetched.
ISO 37301 compliance-management obligations and ISO 22600-2 (cited by HL7) were not fetched as primary texts.
Smart-contract oracle fulfilment, Islamic finance consideration rules, and criminal-law duties are out of the fetched corpus.
DPROD dutyState is an emerging profile, not W3C ODRL core; using it as canonical state without a Dimension declaration would be over-claim.
Hohfeld correlatives are treated only via LegalRuleML Right and FIBO reciprocity, not via a jurisprudence primary text.
conflicts: ODRL fulfilment is binary exercise of an action; UNIDROIT non-performance includes defective and late performance of an otherwise exercised action. Do not collapse these tests.
IAS 37 recognises constructive obligations; US GAAP Topic 450 generally does not under the same model. Overlay fields must not be overwritten across bases.
XACML/HL7/FHIR 'obligation' is a mandated operation or conformance behaviour beside an access or data-handling decision, not a contractual Duty.
ODRL consequence keeps the original duty required; some commercial practices treat liquidated damages as substituting for performance. Record the rule actually adopted.
LegalRuleML Prohibition as [OBL]-p versus ODRL Prohibition as a disjoint Rule subclass: forbearance modelling will not round-trip without an explicit map.
IFRS 15 performance-obligation satisfaction (control transfer) is not the same as ODRL Duty fulfilment or UNIDROIT due performance.
regional_assumptions: UNIDROIT Principles are an international commercial-law restatement, not domestic mandatory law; local civil-code or common-law rules may add consideration, privity or formality requirements.
IAS 37/IFRS 15 overlays assume IFRS reporting; US GAAP and other GAAPs differ on constructive obligations and contingency thresholds.
LegalRuleML encodings are jurisdiction-neutral carriers of jurisdiction-specific norms; jurisdiction-code is an annotation, not a world-law identifier.
ODRL is a web policy language widely used for rights, not a substitute for private-law obligation in courts.
HL7/FHIR obligation codes reflect health-interoperability practice and must not be generalised as legal duties.
adversarial_checks: If an English label 'obligation' is used as a join key across ODRL, XACML and IAS 37, legally distinct senses will be merged; deontic-kind-code is the falsifier.
If fulfilment is stored as a boolean without performance-quality-code, defective and late performance required by UNIDROIT 7.1.1 become invisible.
If due dates are used as identifiers or stored as timezone-naive dates, overdue evaluation is not reproducible across regions.
If consequence duties replace the original duty by default, the instance is not ODRL-compatible even if labelled as such.
If FHIR SHALL-handle-field codes are treated as contractual commitments, healthcare conformance will be misread as legal liability.
If IAS 37 recognition is taken as proof that no obligation exists when outflow is not probable, deontic duties will disappear from operations while still binding at law.
